summary: L-4 cabin on Mount Thompson-Seton in the Flathead National Forest, built in 1931; abandoned in the 1950s, ruins reported in 1984, and listed as gone.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1950s; ruins were reported in 1984. The trail listing names remnants of an old fire lookout but does not say they are the cabin site. No source we read describes the cabin site today.

access.note: Listed as a National Forest trail for hiking. No source we read says whether the cabin site itself is open.

visit.trail_note: 12.2-mile National Forest trail of high difficulty; begins at Whale Creek roads 318 and 1674

events.note: Ruins reported at the site in 1984

evidence.supports: list classes the site as ground, not tower
abandoned in the 1950s; ruins reported in 1984
fire-detection points on high peaks after the 1910 fire season
evidence.quote: After the 1910 fire season, the Forest Service went on the offensive, setting up fire detection points on high peaks

evidence.supports: lookouts added especially in the 1930s; 147 lookouts and towers by 1939
evidence.quote: The Forest built more and more lookouts, especially during the 1930s, until in 1939 there were 147 lookouts and towers on the Flathead National Forest

evidence.supports: National Forest trail, 12.2 miles, high difficulty
trail listed as a National Forest trail
remnants of an old fire lookout named among special attractions
trail begins at Whale Creek roads 318 and 1674

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The site page reports ruins in 1984, while the Forest Association list marks the site simply as gone. Neither source says when the ruins were gone.

sources.title: Trails of the Past: Historical Overview of the Flathead National Forest, Montana, 1800-1960, Chapter 9
Mt.Thompson - Seton Trail in Hungry Horse Montana

notes_for_editor: firelookout.com reports ruins in 1984 and the Forest Association list marks the site gone; the story reports both and does not date the loss of the ruins. Trail facts come from a travel listing on travelmt.com, not a Forest Service page; the Forest Service trail page for the Ninko-Thompson Seton trail, found in search, did not mention the lookout. The access level 'public' refers to the trail, not confirmed for the cabin site. No abandonment year beyond 'the 1950s'.
